bullets.title: LEAD - CLAUDE CODE SHIPPED TWICE IN 24 HOURS: 2.1.275 NOW SYNCS THE SKILLS AND PLUGINS ENABLED ON YOUR claude.ai ACCOUNT INTO EVERY SIGNED-IN TERMINAL SESSION - OUR UNAUDITED SKILL BANK NOW PROPAGATES BY DEFAULT - AND IT CARRIES THE SECOND CREDENTIAL-DISCLOSURE FIX IN TWO CONSECUTIVE RELEASES; 2.1.276 IS A SAME-DAY HOTFIX FOR A REGRESSION 2.1.275 PUT INTO EVERY GATEWAY USER'S SESSION
bullets.summary: Datelines read at the changelog: 2.1.275 "September 17, 2026", 2.1.276 "September 18, 2026". 2.1.275 adds syncing of the skills and plugins enabled on your claude.ai account to terminal sessions signed in with it, opt out with syncClaudeAiSkills:false or syncClaudeAiPlugins:false. It also fixes plugin and marketplace messages, logs and `claude plugin marketplace list` showing a password or token stored in a git, ssh or marketplace URL - the second credential leak fixed in two days, one release after 2.1.274 fixed MCP errors printing ${VAR} secrets. Plus: /rewind in a forked or background session restoring a zero-filled or truncated file; a restored memory file's age note changing between requests after compaction or resume, causing prompt-cache misses; --forward-subagent-text dropping messages of subagents spawned by a context:fork skill; marketplace update deleting a GitHub marketplace's local copy on a failed fetch. 2.1.276 is one line: every request failing with 400 Input tag 'advisor_20260301' when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at a proxy or gateway. Archive grep: 2.1.275 ZERO, 2.1.276 ZERO, syncClaudeAiSkills ZERO, advisor_20260301 ZERO across eighty files.
bullets.how: YES, twice over. The skill sync is the fourth instrument handed to standing item (c) in three days and the first that changes its URGENCY rather than its shape: a corpus we have never audited now propagates automatically into every signed-in terminal, and yesterday's semantic-collapse paper measured what an un-curated bank does to output over weeks. The opt-out flags are named and cost one settings line, so the decision is now curate-or-opt-out, not curate-someday. Second, the credential fix is the second in 48 hours on the same surface, which widens standing item (k) from a one-off grep to two classes: ${VAR} values from pre-2.1.274 MCP errors AND tokens in git/ssh/marketplace URLs from pre-2.1.275 plugin output. Third, the /rewind zero-file fix is silent data loss in the exact mechanism reconcile-before-building exists to survive. Note 2.1.276's shape: a release broke every request behind a gateway and was hotfixed within a day - the vendor-self-index lane is now paying out daily.

bullets.title: GOOGLE SHIPPED ARTIFACT (a). AGENT ANOMALY DETECTION READS THE LOGS AND OpenTelemetry TRACES AGENTS ALREADY EMIT, REASONS OVER THE TOOL CALLS, AND RETURNS A SEVERITY-RANKED FINDING WITH A PLAIN-LANGUAGE RATIONALE - THE INCIDENT LOG WE HAVE DECLINED FOR NINETEEN DAYS, BUILT AS A PRODUCT, GROUNDED IN THE OWASP AGENTIC TOP 10
bullets.summary: Dateline read at the page: Google Developers Blog, SEPT. 16, 2026, Achuth Narayan Rajagopal. Private Preview on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, ADK 1.2+. Quoted framing: "The real damage often happens in sessions that look benign on the surface... Because nothing failed outright, the session clears the usual metrics-based evaluations without any second look." Mechanism: a lightweight statistical pass over all traffic flags outlier sessions, an LLM reasoning layer examines flagged ones in full, a third layer reconstructs individual tool calls. Runs asynchronously, out of band, zero added runtime latency. Detectors map to named OWASP Agentic Top 10 (2026) categories - tool misuse ASI02, identity and privilege abuse ASI03, cascading failures ASI08, rogue agents ASI10 - plus resource exhaustion and token-usage escalation. Findings publish to Security Command Center with severity, probability and recommended fixes, and are pullable by API so an ADK callback can block later tool calls above a threshold. Worked example: an inventory agent paged the whole catalogue in 100-item offset jumps, threw no error, broke no policy, and came back Resource exhaustion, Critical, 95%. Archive grep: Agent Anomaly ZERO, OWASP Agentic ZERO, Security Command Center ZERO, ASI02 ZERO across eighty files.
bullets.how: YES, and the most uncomfortable bullet of the month. Artifact (a), the incident log, is on its twentieth day with zero rows and accumulated three independent justifications in a single day on 17 Sep. This is that artifact, specified by someone else, on a competitor's stack, at a maturity we have not started. Two things make it actionable rather than merely embarrassing: the input it consumes is OpenTelemetry traces the agents already emit, and Claude Code 2.1.274 shipped claude_code.managed_settings_resolved and the effort span attribute the day before yesterday - so the emitting half of item (b) is live on OUR stack and the missing half is a place to put it and something that reads it. We are not adopting Google's platform; we are taking its output shape - severity, probability, plain-language rationale, recommended fix, API-pullable - as the schema for our own.

bullets.title: arXiv MEASURED THE DEFECT THIS REPORT NAMED YESTERDAY. "VERIFICATION-STATUS LAUNDERING": WHEN A HANDOFF KEEPS THE CLAIM THAT AN ACTION WAS AUTHORISED BUT DROPS THE FACT THAT NOBODY VERIFIED IT, MONITOR APPROVAL OF RISKY ACTIONS GOES FROM 9% TO 98% - AND THE COMPONENT THAT STRIPS THE STATUS MOST RELIABLY IS THE MEMORY COMPRESSOR
bullets.summary: Dateline honesty: 2609.20211 appeared in today's cs.MA listing (Fri 18 Sep) but its submission history reads 25 Jul 2026 - new to the listing, not new to the world. Safety monitors judge actions from summaries and stored handoffs rather than original evidence, so "the handoff preserves the claim that an action is authorized while losing the fact that the claim was never verified." Holding the action and the authorisation proposition fixed and removing only the unverified-provenance framing raises approval for risky actions from 5% to 60% on Llama-3.1-8B and from 9% to 98% on Qwen2.5-14B, with similar shifts on two hosted models. It emerges without an attacker: "Summarizers frequently weaken the status, memory compressors often remove it," and a full proposer-summariser-memory-monitor pipeline pushes risky approval to 57-81% across three downstream monitors. Instructing the monitor to reject unverified authorisation is NOT a reliable cross-model fix - some stay vulnerable, others start refusing legitimate work. The prescription is structural: carry authorization provenance as structured state attached to the claim throughout the pipeline. Companion: 2609.18820 Compositional Policy Violations (17 Sep) - step-level compliance passes while the COMPOSITION of compliant steps violates policy; 2609.19502 Reputation as Community Memory for the Agentic Web (18 Sep). Archive grep: 2609.20211 ZERO, verification-status laundering ZERO, 2609.18820 ZERO, 2609.19502 ZERO across eighty files.
bullets.how: YES, and a direct hit on two things we run. We compact. We summarise into praxis-inbox.md and into standing lists. We hand off between Cowork, Hermes and the worker queue, and the receiver sees the summary, not the evidence - that is the exact pipeline shape measured here, and reconcile-before-building exists because we already watched compaction drop record of completed work. It retires the vocabulary argument from 17 Sep: decision laundering was the name for a gate certifying work nobody looked at; verification-status laundering is the measured mechanism, and the number to keep is that the MEMORY COMPRESSOR is the worst offender. Consequence for item (j): a gate that emits a pass is emitting a claim, and if the pass travels without its evidence the next stage reads silence as endorsement. The exit code must carry provenance, not just a verdict. vironbox-provenance-gate is the skill we already own that says this; this paper is its citation.

bullets.title: GOVERNANCE STACK, DAY SIX: GOOGLE DEEPMIND LAUNCHED AN INSTITUTE AND HASSABIS USED IT TO PROPOSE A US-LED FRONTIER STANDARDS BODY WITH "HELD-OUT" EVALUATIONS - UNDISCLOSED TESTS SPECIFICALLY SO LABS CANNOT TAILOR MODELS TO THE EVAL THEY WILL BE GRADED ON
bullets.summary: Dateline read at the page: TechCrunch, article:published_time 2026-09-17T23:21:17+00:00, Aditya Mehta. Directors Shane Legg, James Manyika and Demis Hassabis, Legg as managing editor, four inaugural essays. Hassabis's framework: developers submit models voluntarily for review up to 30 days before release, and once the system proves itself, passing could become a REQUIREMENT for US deployment; assessments start in consultation with the labs but move to independent, undisclosed "held-out" tests, and the framework could be "ratcheted up if the seriousness of the situation demands," up to a coordinated slowdown among frontier developers. The Shah-Dragan essay argues the shrinking window into a model's step-by-step reasoning is not inevitable and floats limiting "opaque serial depth" - the sequential computation a model may perform without producing a readable trace - or forcing developers to prove less transparent systems remain monitorable. Context given at the page: this follows industry leaders endorsing parts of Amodei's 12 Sep call to "pace" frontier development. Archive grep: DeepMind Institute ZERO, Shane Legg ZERO, held-out ZERO, opaque serial depth ZERO, reasoning transparency ZERO across eighty files.
bullets.how: MAYBE - no operational action today, one idea worth stealing. The governance stack tracked since 12 Sep now reads detect / certify / recover / govern / monitor / and now GRADE WITH TESTS THE GRADED PARTY HAS NEVER SEEN. That last rung is the sharpest available critique of our own AAIR number: a score computed from a published method is a score a client can be optimised toward, and a stamp you can teach to is a stamp whose provenance has been laundered - which is bullet 3 at industry scale. The cheap version for us is not a new product: hold back a slice of the question corpus from the answer-shaping loop so the re-measure is scored on questions the pages were never written against. That is a one-file change to how mallard-b9-visibility splits its corpus, and it would make an AAIR delta mean something it does not currently mean.

praxis_lesson: THREE OF TODAY'S FIVE ITEMS ARE ONE DEFECT AT THREE ALTITUDES, AND IT IS THE DEFECT WE RUN ON. A claim travels; its provenance does not; the receiver reads silence as endorsement. arXiv measured it at the pipeline layer - strip the unverified-provenance framing and monitor approval of risky actions goes 9% to 98%, with the MEMORY COMPRESSOR identified as the component that most reliably removes the status, and a full proposer-summariser-memory-monitor chain landing at 57-81%. Google productised the remedy at the session layer: Agent Anomaly Detection does not trust the agent's summary of its own session, it re-reads the traces and tool calls and reconstructs what actually happened. Hassabis proposed it at the industry layer: held-out evaluations, undisclosed specifically because a test whose contents the graded party knows is a certificate whose provenance has been laundered. Our own instance is exact and unflattering: we compact, we summarise into standing lists and praxis blocks, and we hand off between Cowork, Hermes and the worker queue - and at every one of those boundaries the receiver gets the claim and not the evidence. The correction is one sentence and it is already the name of a skill we own: a gate must emit provenance, not a verdict. SECOND, THE ACCOUNT ON ARTIFACT (a): on 17 Sep this report concluded that after three justifications in one day and nineteen days of no rows, the honest statement was that the incident log is being DECLINED, not missing. Today a vendor shipped it - same input (OpenTelemetry traces the agents already emit), same output (severity, probability, plain-language rationale, recommended fix), on a platform we do not use. The excuse that survived nineteen days was never "we don't know how"; it is now demonstrably "we have not spent the hour," and the emitting half went live on our own stack two days ago in 2.1.274. THIRD, THE METHOD NOTE, WHICH KEEPS PAYING: the vendor-self-index lane produced the lead for the third consecutive fire - 2.1.276 shipped TODAY and the changelog had it before any aggregator did. The same discipline killed today's most plausible-looking item: Google's MCP-stateless post, served as 17 Sep, reads AUG. 5 at the page and is already in 47 of our 80 files. The security-disclosure lane named yesterday is still unwritten and produced nothing today - which is not evidence it is unnecessary, only that it has not been built.
